key_insight: The paper proposes that deep learning generalization is limited by an entropic threshold: a network learns only when data-manifold entropy exceeds the topological complexity of the target boundary, adjusted by weight-space entropy.
engineering_relevance: If valid, this framework could guide model design and optimization by identifying when overparameterized networks are likely to memorize versus generalize, and by motivating entropy-aware training methods.
method: Introduces the Entropic Learnability Horizon (ELH) as a bound on learnability.
States the Shannon-Topological Bottleneck Theorem to explain a phase transition into informational frustration.
Proposes Entropic Gradient Descent (EGD) to dynamically manage weight entropy during training.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical framework and algorithmic proposal, but does not report concrete datasets, experimental benchmarks, or quantitative evaluation results.
watch_item: The main concern is that the claims are largely theoretical and depend on definitions of entropy and topology that may be difficult to measure or validate in practical deep learning systems.
paper_title: Informational Frustration in Neural Manifolds: Shannon Bottlenecks and the Limits of Learnability
